title: Obfuscation Budget: How Hard Is It to Hide from a Linear Probe?

original_idea.body:
# Obfuscation Budget: How Hard Is It to Hide from a Linear Probe?

Apply increasing simple prompt obfuscation (synonym swaps, base64, leetspeak, spacing) to known jailbreaks against a trained linear probe and measure the tradeoff between probe-evasion rate and StrongREJECT response quality, producing an obfuscation cost curve. Small probe + inference (arXiv:2412.09565).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Level 4: strong chain — quantifying evasion-vs-quality cost informs whether probe defenses hold, a concrete detection-scaling open problem.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Level 4: train a linear probe + apply obfuscations + StrongREJECT scoring; activation extraction needs ML fundamentals, guided.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Level 5: tightly scoped single experiment (obfuscation cost curve) with clear success criteria.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Level 4: open model + small probe, no internal access, third-party robustness auditing labs underweight.

low_compute.reasoning: Linear probe + inference on one open model, single consumer GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Obfuscated activations studied; the quantified evasion-vs-quality cost curve for simple obfuscations may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Obfuscation attacks known; the cost-curve quantification is plausibly open.
